objective: Compare what Claude Code's built-in git instructions give the model (commit and PR workflow guidance, safety rules, git status snapshot) with what HolyAgent's own version-control instructions give the root and specialists, and list concrete gaps HolyAgent should cover now that setup turns the built-in ones off.
scope: HolyAgent's VCS text: packages/integrations/claude/src (root and specialist section files, hooks that add VCS context), docs/commit-authorship.md, docs/hooks.md, the holyagent vcs commit/pr implementation in packages/runtime.

Claude Code's built-in git guidance: what includeGitInstructions removes (from Claude Code docs or the plugin's own notes; if the exact text is not available locally, say so and work from documented behavior).
constraints: Read-only. For each gap give the rule Claude Code had, whether HolyAgent covers it (path:line), and a one-sentence proposed instruction for HolyAgent. Mark gaps that matter for safety (e.g. never skip hooks, never amend others' commits, never commit secrets, check status/diff before commit) separately from nice-to-haves.
Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 500 words.
